user.title: Wind Forecast Finland
user.description: Set up the hub. Only one is needed — after creating it, add a Fingrid and/or FMI source (and optionally a combined view) from the integration's page.

abort.already_configured: Wind Forecast Finland is already configured — only one hub is needed.

init.title: Fingrid wind forecast
init.description: Fingrid dataset 245 publishes Finland's wind-generation forecast in 15-minute buckets. Your key is validated with a small live test-fetch before this source is saved.

data_description.api_key: Free to obtain at https://data.fingrid.fi — register, then create an API key with access to open datasets. Dataset 245 (wind power generation forecast) needs no special permission beyond a basic account.
data_description.update_interval: How often to poll Fingrid, in minutes (floor 5 — Fingrid's own data refreshes roughly every 15 minutes, so polling much faster just wastes your rate limit).
data_description.stale_after_hours: How long without a successful fetch before this source is flagged stale (drives the diagnostic stale sensor and, after a longer prolonged outage, a repair issue).
data_description.lookback_hours: How many hours of already-past forecast buckets to keep fetching/displaying, for context on dashboards.
data_description.horizon_hours: How many hours ahead to fetch. Fingrid typically publishes out to roughly 36-74 hours depending on the dataset run.

error.invalid_api_key: That API key was rejected by Fingrid (401/403). Double-check it at https://data.fingrid.fi.
error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach Fingrid to validate the key (timeout or network error). Check connectivity and try again.

abort.already_configured: A Fingrid source is already configured for this hub — only one is needed.

init.title: FMI wind forecast
init.description: The Finnish Meteorological Institute publishes an hourly Finland wind-power forecast on a public CDN endpoint — no API key needed.

data_description.update_interval: How often to poll the FMI CDN, in minutes (floor 5 — FMI's own forecast refreshes roughly every 15-60 minutes).
data_description.stale_after_hours: How long without a successful fetch before this source is flagged stale (drives the diagnostic stale sensor and, after a longer prolonged outage, a repair issue).

abort.already_configured: An FMI source is already configured for this hub — only one is needed.

init.title: Combined wind forecast
init.description: Picks one source as primary and, optionally, fills true gaps in it from a secondary source. The two forecasts are never averaged — their methodologies disagree, so blending would match neither.

data.gap_fill: Fill gaps from the secondary source

data_description.primary: The source whose forecast wins whenever both sources cover the same hour.
data_description.secondary: Used only to fill hours the primary source doesn't cover (a real gap, e.g. an outage or a shorter horizon) — never to average with the primary.
data_description.gap_fill: When off, the combined view is a clean passthrough of the primary source only (still falls back to cache the same way a single source does).

abort.already_configured: A combined view is already configured for this hub — only one is needed.
abort.no_sources: Add a Fingrid and/or FMI source first — the combined view needs at least one to merge.

source_stale.title: Wind Forecast Finland: {source} forecast stale
source_stale.description: The {source} source hasn't fetched successfully in a while, so it's serving an old cached forecast (or none at all). Check connectivity/API key and the Home Assistant logs. This clears automatically once a fetch succeeds again.
